result.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved substantial progress across many domains, but training an agent \textit{tabula rasa} remains highly sample-inefficient. A common remedy is to initialize the agent using a neural network pretrained on demonstrations. However, collecting demonstrations is expensive, and the demonstrations themselves can be suboptimal. In this work, we use a large language model (LLM) to generate an advice policy that produces demonstration data with effectively no human cost. We use this data to warmstart a DQN agent, and use the advice policy itself to guide exploration during training. Because LLM-generated advice is often suboptimal, we further introduce a value warmstart method that initializes the agent to recognize promising states from the advice policy's behavior, without directly copying its actions. To characterize the robustness of this method, we systematically perturb individual sub-skills of an LLM-generated advice policy for a long-horizon, sparse-reward task. Degraded advice still meaningfully accelerates learning relative to unaided baselines. These results suggest that LLM-generated advice, though suboptimal, can be a cheap alternative to costly human demonstrations.

AI.brief_summary: 用 LLM 生成「建议策略」以零人工成本产出示范数据，据此 warmstart DQN 并在训练中引导探索；由于建议常次优，提出只初始化价值、不直接复制动作的 value warmstart，并在长时稀疏奖励任务上系统性退化各子技能以检验稳健性。
AI.relevance_reason: 「从次优建议中提取状态价值而非模仿动作」可能为 LVR 中利用次优推理轨迹做监督、避免直接对齐错误 latent 轨迹提供线索，可供核查；但该文任务是纯 RL 控制，与视觉推理状态无直接证据。
